newsitem.title: UK: Intervention still needed after EMU - EC's Carre.
newsitem.headline: Intervention still needed after EMU - EC's Carre.

text.p: Intervention will still be necessary once the single European currency is established, said Herve de Carre, European Commission director for monetary matters.

The so-called "pre-ins", or currencies that will not yet be part of the single currency at its scheduled start on January 1, 1999, are likely to be exposed to wide fluctuations against the euro, said Carre.
"Pre-in currencies will have relatively wide fluctuation margin rates against the euro," Carre told a conference on monetary union in London.

But he said closer links will be possible. "In order to avoid speculation the sustainability of central rates will be the subject of continued surveillance, and the realignment of central rates when necessary will be effected in a timely manner," he said.
"Intervention will remain an important feature of the new mechanism," he said. He added, however, the emphasis will be on sound economic management and the need to provide exchange rate stability.
The aim of ERM 2 was two-fold, firstly to prepare the "pre-ins" for participation in the euro area, said Carre.
Secondly, its aim was to exploit the exchange rate stability by creating links between euro members and those not yet members.
